chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Show structure and benefit performances
summary: The band played dance sets, two shows a night, and benefit shows before work as part of the club's civic policy.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: WILLARD: And so Duke's band played all the music for the show?
BROWN
I don't think -- I think that for the show, most of
the music was written by these other writers.
But in the course of an evening--
(inaudible).
Between the show, see, we played on stage for dancing and things. All that was Ellington's part.
WILLARD: Was there more than one show a night?
There was two shows a night, plus always a benefit show before we went off to work.
Before you went --
We'd go out -- we'd go out to different places and do a benefit show.
For what kind of --
They'd
We'd take the whole show. I don't know -- it was just that -- the policy of the Cotton Club management to contribute to city functions. Oh a lot of functions around.
WILLARD: Were you paid extra for that or was that part of the job?
BROWN: Yeah.
WILLARD: Was that in the daytime or early evening?
Get there about 7:00 o'clock. And the first show didn't go on -- the regular show didn't go on until about 10:00 10:30 -- something like that. The last went on about 2:30.
MS. WILLARD: You said you would go out and play a benefit, does that mean not on the premises of the
Cotton Club.
~A bus and we'd go maybe to the Astor or we'd go to this club or we'd go to that hall or places like that.
